sentences.en: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Friedrich Froebel.
sentences.zh: 很久很久以前，有一个叫弗里德里希·福禄贝尔的男孩。

sentences.en: His early life reads like one of those dark, old German fairy tales.
sentences.zh: 他早年的生活读起来就像那些阴郁的古老德国童话。

sentences.en: His mother died in 1783, right after he was born.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲在他出生后不久的1783年就去世了。

sentences.en: And so Friedrich Froebel had a lonely childhood.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗里德里希·福禄贝尔度过了一个孤独的童年。

sentences.en: He spent his days in the woods, looking at trees and rocks and flowers,
sentences.zh: 他整天待在树林里，观察树木、岩石和花朵，

sentences.en: wandering the dense forests of Thuringia in what was then Prussia.
sentences.zh: 漫步在当时属于普鲁士的图林根茂密森林中。

sentences.en: It's a lush region, sometimes referred to today as Das Grüne Herz Deutschlands,
sentences.zh: 那是一个郁郁葱葱的地区，今天有时被称为“德国的绿色心脏”，
那是库尔特·科尔斯塔德。

sentences.en: I actually lived near Thuringia when I was a kid,
sentences.zh: 我小时候其实住在图林根附近，

sentences.en: and the forests there are einfach zauberhaft, simply magical.
sentences.zh: 那里的森林简直是“神奇的”，非常迷人。

sentences.en: And I can really see how Froebel became enthralled.
sentences.zh: 我真的能理解福禄贝尔是如何被它迷住的。

sentences.en: He looked at rocks, he studied the trees, he worked with a forester for a while,
sentences.zh: 他观察岩石，研究树木，还曾与一位林务员一起工作过一段时间，
他曾是一名林务员学徒。

sentences.en: He's an author who studied Friedrich Froebel for years.
sentences.zh: 他是一位研究弗里德里希·福禄贝尔多年的作家。

sentences.en: Brosterman says that Froebel worked for a time as a land surveyor,
sentences.zh: 布罗斯特曼说，福禄贝尔曾做过一段时间的土地测量员，

sentences.en: and even served in the military.
He was skilled at drafting and geometry,
and at one point became convinced he should be an architect.
sentences.zh: 一度确信自己应该成为一名建筑师。

sentences.en: He did everything you need to become an architect.
sentences.zh: 他做了成为建筑师所需的一切准备。

sentences.en: He took all the right classes.
But he didn't become an architect.
sentences.zh: 但他最终没有成为建筑师。

sentences.en: A friend convinced him to become an educator instead.
sentences.zh: 一位朋友说服他转而成为了一名教育家。

sentences.en: And in changing course, Froebel arguably ended up having more influence
sentences.zh: 而通过这次转型，福禄贝尔最终在建筑和设计领域产生的影响力，

sentences.en: in the world of architecture and design than any single architect.
sentences.zh: 可以说超过了任何一位单一的建筑师。

sentences.en: And that's because Friedrich Froebel created kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 这是因为弗里德里希·福禄贝尔创造了幼儿园。

sentences.en: I believe kindergarten had a tremendous influence on the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 我相信幼儿园对20世纪产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: It impacted all parts of society, of course, including art and architecture.
sentences.zh: 它当然影响了社会的各个方面，包括艺术和建筑。

sentences.en: If you've ever looked at a piece of abstract art or modernist architecture and thought,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经看过一件抽象艺术品或现代主义建筑，并心想：

sentences.en: my kindergartner could have made that.
sentences.zh: “我上幼儿园的孩子也能做出这种东西。”

sentences.en: Well, that may be more true than you realize.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能比你意识到的更真实。

sentences.en: The kindergarten was the product of Froebel's decades of experience in a wide range of fields.
sentences.zh: 幼儿园是福禄贝尔在多个领域数十年经验的结晶。

sentences.en: But the foundations of it were built on the principles of Johann Pestalozzi.
sentences.zh: 但它的基础建立在约翰·裴斯泰洛齐的原则之上。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi is considered the father of modern education,
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐被认为是现代教育之父，

sentences.en: which basically means they will learn better if you treat them well,
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着如果你善待孩子，他们会学得更好，

sentences.en: rather than hit them with sticks, you know.
sentences.zh: 而不是用棍子打他们，你懂的。

sentences.en: In addition to the whole not hitting kids with sticks thing,
sentences.zh: 除了“不拿棍子打孩子”这件事之外，

sentences.en: Pestalozzi emphasized physical activity and active learning
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐强调体育活动和主动学习，
而不是死记硬背和机械重复。

sentences.en: And in particular, he felt that kids should draw.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他认为孩子们应该画画。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi was an early childhood educator
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐是一位幼儿教育家，

sentences.en: who had incorporated pedagogical drawings in the curriculum.
sentences.zh: 他将教学绘画纳入了课程体系。

sentences.en: That's author and Cooper Union professor Tamar Zinger.
sentences.zh: 那是作家兼库珀联盟教授塔玛·辛格。

sentences.en: And basically, he is one of the first who thought that drawing
sentences.zh: 基本上，他是最早认为绘画

sentences.en: should be part of any school curriculum
sentences.zh: 应该成为任何学校课程的一部分，

sentences.en: and should be taught to the very, very young.
sentences.zh: 并且应该教给非常非常年幼的孩子的人之一。

sentences.en: Froebel worked for a time at a school based on these principles,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔曾在一所基于这些原则的学校工作过一段时间，

sentences.en: and he built on what he learned from Pestalozzi,
sentences.zh: 他在裴斯泰洛齐所学的基础上，

sentences.en: incorporating his own ideas along the way about how children should be taught.
sentences.zh: 融入了自己关于应该如何教育孩子的想法。

sentences.en: Pestalozzi was especially busy with breaking down the two-dimensional world,
sentences.zh: 裴斯泰洛齐特别致力于解析二维世界，

sentences.en: but what Froebel did is break down the three-dimensional world.
sentences.zh: 但福禄贝尔所做的是解析三维世界。

sentences.en: Froebel realized he wanted kids to go beyond just drawing lines on pages.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔意识到他希望孩子们不仅仅是在纸上画线。

sentences.en: He wanted them to learn through the physical manipulation of objects.
sentences.zh: 他希望他们通过对物体的物理操纵来学习。

sentences.en: Froebel wanted children to play with toys,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔希望孩子们玩玩具，

sentences.en: objects designed and crafted specifically for educational play.
sentences.zh: 即专门为教育性游戏设计和制作的物体。

sentences.en: Now, this doesn't sound that unusual today,
sentences.zh: 现在，这在今天听起来并不稀奇，

sentences.en: but it really was back in the early 1800s.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪初，这确实非常罕见。

sentences.en: Children used to go to work with their parents.
sentences.zh: 孩子们过去常常和父母一起去工作。

sentences.en: They used to sit by their parents' side,
sentences.zh: 他们过去常常坐在父母身边，

sentences.en: and they would play with the detritus of the parents' work.
sentences.zh: 玩父母工作时留下的废料。

sentences.en: I mean, for example, the candle maker would make wax figurines
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，例如，蜡烛制造商会用剩下的蜡

sentences.en: The wooden blocks were only made from the leftover wood from the carpenter.
sentences.zh: 木块只是用木匠剩下的木头制成的。

sentences.en: So it was always from the leftover material.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是来自剩余的材料。

sentences.en: Froebel wanted to build real educational intent into objects of play,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔想把真正的教育意图融入到游戏物体中，

sentences.en: but it took him decades to come to this key realization,
sentences.zh: 但他花了数十年时间才得出这个关键的认识，

sentences.en: and a lot of time observing children and nature.
sentences.zh: 并花费大量时间观察儿童和自然。

sentences.en: He was put in charge of an orphanage for a while,
sentences.zh: 他曾负责管理一家孤儿院一段时间，

sentences.en: But he also studied the natural sciences,
sentences.zh: 但他还研究了自然科学，

sentences.en: in particular the emerging discipline of crystallography.
sentences.zh: 特别是当时新兴的晶体学学科。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out that the man who invented kindergarten
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，发明幼儿园的那个人

sentences.en: He worked with the foremost crystallographer of the time in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他在柏林与当时最顶尖的晶体学家一起工作。

sentences.en: Where most people saw nature in big, flowing, organic shapes
sentences.zh: 大多数人看到的是大自然中流动、有机的形状，

sentences.en: like hills and plants and animals,
Froebel zoomed in to study the straight lines
sentences.zh: 而福禄贝尔则聚焦于研究直线

sentences.en: and the geometric forms of crystals.
To try to understand how the physical world around him is actually made.
sentences.zh: 试图理解他周围的物理世界实际上是如何构成的。

sentences.en: And Froebel came to see crystal structures
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔开始将晶体结构

sentences.en: as the building blocks of reality.
And this alchemy of crystals and the teaching of Pestalozzi
sentences.zh: 而这种晶体炼金术、裴斯泰洛齐的教学法

sentences.en: and a childhood alone in the woods
sentences.zh: 以及独自在树林中度过的童年，

sentences.en: all crystallized into a solid vision.
sentences.zh: 最终都结晶成了一个坚实的愿景。

sentences.en: In 1837, when he was 55 years old,
Froebel founded the very first kindergarten
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔在德国巴特布兰肯堡

sentences.en: And his intention was to create an educational system
for children who could not yet read or write.
sentences.zh: 还不会读写的孩子建立一套教育体系。

sentences.en: So he thought to use geometric forms
sentences.zh: 所以他想到利用几何图形，

sentences.en: as a way to teach complex and simple lessons

sentences.zh: 来教授复杂和简单课程的方式。

sentences.en: you can teach kids a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 你就能教给孩子们很多东西。

sentences.en: The word kindergarten cleverly encompassed two different ideas.
sentences.zh: “幼儿园”（Kindergarten）这个词巧妙地涵盖了两个不同的概念。

sentences.en: Kids would play in and learn from nature,
sentences.zh: 孩子们会在大自然中玩耍并从中学习，

sentences.en: but they would also themselves be nurtured and nourished
sentences.zh: 但他们自己也会像花园里的植物一样，

sentences.en: And the key to it all was a set of
sentences.zh: 而这一切的关键是一套
看起来简单得令人难以置信的玩具。
这些就是福禄贝尔的“恩物”。

sentences.en: They're called gifts because they were to draw out the gifts
sentences.zh: 它们被称为“恩物”，因为它们旨在引出孩子们

sentences.en: In German, of course, the phrase
Froebel's gifts is rolled together into a single word.
sentences.zh: “福禄贝尔的恩物”这个词组被合并成了一个词。

sentences.en: Froebel's gifts were meant to be given in a particular order,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔的恩物需要按特定的顺序给予，

sentences.en: the toys growing more complex over time,
sentences.zh: 玩具随着时间的推移变得越来越复杂，
在过程中教授关于形状、

sentences.en: structure, and perception along the way.
sentences.zh: 结构和感知的不同课程。

sentences.en: The first of Froebel's gifts was a soft, knitted ball.
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔的第一件恩物是一个柔软的针织球。

sentences.en: And it's basically the first gift a child could get
sentences.zh: 它基本上是孩子在六周大时

sentences.en: at the age of six weeks.
sentences.zh: 可以得到的第一件礼物。

sentences.en: Then the child would graduate to another ball,
sentences.zh: 然后孩子会进阶到另一个球，

sentences.en: roughly the same size as the firSt.
But this one is not soft.
And then they are given the cube.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会得到一个立方体。

sentences.en: And the cube is an opposite.
Kids are asked to enumerate the differences between the two.
sentences.zh: 孩子们被要求列举两者之间的差异。

sentences.en: And then they get a cylinder,
sentences.zh: 然后他们会得到一个圆柱体，

sentences.en: which combines elements of both the ball and the cube.
sentences.zh: 它结合了球体和立方体的元素。

sentences.en: And it blows their little minds.
sentences.zh: 这让孩子们的小脑袋瓜大开眼界。

sentences.en: Each new gift would get more and more interactive
sentences.zh: 每一件新的恩物都会变得越来越具有互动性

sentences.en: Some were designed to be hung from a string
sentences.zh: 有些被设计成用绳子悬挂起来，

sentences.en: some very interesting forms are created
sentences.zh: 会产生一些非常有趣的形态，

sentences.en: that are not visible when the form is stationary.
sentences.zh: 这些形态在物体静止时是看不见的。

sentences.en: looks like a cylinder when you spin it around fast enough.
sentences.zh: 当你旋转得足够快时，它看起来就像一个圆柱体。

sentences.en: He wants the children to start to see
sentences.zh: 他希望孩子们开始看到，

sentences.en: that there are some invisible parts

sentences.zh: 还包含着一些不可见的部分。

sentences.en: Next up came objects made up of smaller objects,
sentences.zh: 接下来出现的是由更小的物体组成的物体。

sentences.en: like a cube that breaks down into a bunch of little cubes.
sentences.zh: 就像一个能拆解成一堆小方块的立方体。

sentences.en: And then the toys would shift from being about perception
sentences.zh: 随后，玩具的重点将从感知

sentences.en: Blocks gave way to paper, string, wire,
sentences.zh: 积木让位于纸张、绳子、金属丝、

sentences.en: little sticks and peas that could be connected

sentences.zh: 并堆叠成各种结构的小棍和豌豆。

sentences.en: The objects would get more abstract and creative,
sentences.zh: 这些物体变得更加抽象和具有创造性，

sentences.en: The last is really just working freely with clay.
sentences.zh: 最后一课其实就是自由地使用粘土。

sentences.en: Clay being the most malleable of all.
sentences.zh: 粘土是所有材料中最具可塑性的。

sentences.en: And there's a whole range of things
a child could build with it.
sentences.zh: 构建出各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: But even at this final stage,
sentences.zh: 但即使是在这最后阶段，

sentences.en: this wasn't the kind of creative free-for-all
sentences.zh: 这也不是我们通常认为的那种

sentences.en: we tend to associate with childhood play.
sentences.zh: 童年游戏中的那种自由创作。

sentences.en: Frobel had children sitting at desks,
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔让孩子们坐在课桌前，

sentences.en: little workstations with grids laid out on them.
sentences.zh: 在铺设了网格的小工作台上操作。

sentences.en: The fact that the table has an underlying grid
sentences.zh: 桌子上有底层网格这一事实，

sentences.en: is very much at the root of the directed play.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是这种引导式游戏的根源。
并且存在一种潜在的秩序。

sentences.en: And so in this very structured,
sentences.zh: 因此，以这种非常结构化、

sentences.en: the gifts encourage students to think abstractly
sentences.zh: 这些“恩物”鼓励学生进行抽象思考，

sentences.en: and to relate ideas, objects, and symbols.
sentences.zh: 并将思想、物体和符号联系起来。

sentences.en: A set of blocks could be used to teach counting.
sentences.zh: 一套积木可以用来教数数。

sentences.en: Then the child could use those same blocks
sentences.zh: 然后孩子可以用同样的积木

sentences.en: and then tell stories of a family living in that house.
sentences.zh: 并讲述住在那所房子里的一家人的故事。

sentences.en: So they were modeling the world in different ways,
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在以不同的方式模拟世界，

sentences.en: all using the same set of objects.
sentences.zh: 而使用的都是同一套物体。

sentences.en: The children realized that they can create new shapes
sentences.zh: 孩子们意识到他们可以创造出新的形状，

sentences.en: and new forms that they create on top of the gridded table.
sentences.zh: 以及在网格桌上创造出新的形式。
这些幼儿园不仅仅是学校。

sentences.en: without all the sex and drugs and clove cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 只是没有那些性、毒品和丁香烟。

sentences.en: They were places that taught about shape and form and color.
sentences.zh: 它们是教授形状、形式和色彩的地方。

sentences.en: And when kindergarten graduates went out into the world,
sentences.zh: 当幼儿园毕业生走向世界时，

is really different than the kind of art
sentences.zh: 与孩子们上过幼儿园之后

sentences.zh: 创作的艺术类型确实不同。
表现主义、立体主义和超现实主义艺术家，

sentences.en: like Paul Klee and Vasily Kandinsky
sentences.zh: 如保罗·克利和瓦西里·康定斯基，
其他人，比如皮特·蒙德里安，
则是作为教师接触到了福禄贝尔教学法。

sentences.zh: 当你审视他们的许多作品时，

sentences.zh: 再对照幼儿园教师指南中的插图，
你会发现这种相似性令人惊叹。
幼儿园也影响了设计师。

sentences.en: Walter Gropius started the Bauhaus in 1919.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·格罗皮乌斯于1919年创办了包豪斯。

sentences.en: Gropius decided to hire a kindergarten teacher
sentences.zh: 格罗皮乌斯决定聘请一位幼儿园老师，

sentences.en: as the first hire of this famous school of design.
sentences.zh: 作为这所著名设计学院的第一位雇员。

sentences.en: So the Bauhaus had its adult design students
sentences.zh: 因此，包豪斯的成年设计学生们

sentences.en: much like those found in kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 与幼儿园里的练习非常相似。

sentences.en: And the effects of Frobel's work on design education
sentences.zh: 福禄贝尔的工作对设计教育的影响，

sentences.en: And some of his most explicit and direct influences
sentences.zh: 他最明确和直接的影响，

sentences.en: can be found among the world's most famous architects.
sentences.zh: 可以在世界上最著名的建筑师身上找到。

sentences.zh: 美国建筑师弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特，

sentences.en: is the great child of the kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 就是幼儿园的伟大产物。

sentences.zh: 在赖特所做的一切中，你都能找到幼儿园的影子。

sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特出生于1867年，

sentences.zh: 大约在幼儿园开始在美国

sentences.zh: 他的母亲参加过幼儿园教育课程。

sentences.zh: 但他回忆说，当他年轻时，

sentences.zh: 母亲带回家一套福禄贝尔“恩物”。

sentences.zh: 赖特说，在他得到福禄贝尔“恩物”的那一刻，

sentences.zh: 我坐在那张小小的幼儿园桌子旁，

sentences.zh: 和枫木积木才是最重要的。

sentences.zh: 至今，这一切仍刻在我的指尖。”

But he did attend Frobelian schools in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在瑞士上过福禄贝尔学校。
